title: Reading lab: Romans 8:1–4
subtitle: Trace assertion, explanation, and purpose in epistle prose.
overview: Romans 8:1–4 begins with a concise assertion, grounds it with γάρ, and develops its purpose through ἵνα. Keep this argument visible as you parse the dense phrases.
Read each prepositional and genitive phrase as a relationship inside the argument, not as an isolated theological slogan.

items.grc: οὐδὲν ἄρα νῦν κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
items.en: Therefore there is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus.

items.grc: ἵνα τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ νόμου πληρωθῇ ἐν ἡμῖν τοῖς μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦσιν.
items.en: So that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us who do not walk according to the flesh.
